audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[].side read Naafiri, then Skill on all six remaining rows, while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Skill/Naafiri/Naafiri/Naafiri/Naafiri/Ekko/Ekko. The page answered 'who wins level 1' two different ways.
audit.why: At rank 1 both Q cooldowns are 9s, but Naafiri's Darkin Daggers is 900 range with packmates leaping on the target while Ekko's E is a 325-range dash — level 1 is a skill row, and her Eviscerate (11s) plus The Call of the Pack (26s) own levels 2-5 until Chronobreak lands.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side = Skill, phases[1..4].side = Naafiri, phases[5..6].side = Ekko, matching win[] and the packet; every flipped why rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text never named a Naafiri ability or a cooldown; level 6 was described as a turning point without saying that Hounds' Pursuit lands at the same time.
audit.why: enemyKit R Hounds' Pursuit 110/95/80s, recastable, second cast shields; ownerKit R Chronobreak 110/80/50s. Both ults arrive at 6, so the spike is a trade of ultimates, not a free flip.
audit.corrected: Spikes now name Hounds' Pursuit's 110s rank-1 cooldown against Chronobreak's 110s, and the first-item row keys off Eviscerate's 11s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was absent: Naafiri has three separate untargetable windows — The Call of the Pack (W), Eviscerate (E) and Hounds' Pursuit (R) — so a timed Ekko commit can hit nothing at all. Her Eviscerate also heals her packmates, and the R recast shields her.
audit.why: enemyKit flags: W untargetable; E untargetable + heal + dash; R untargetable + shield + slow + revealsStealth. These are exactly the three missingInteractions rules for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, dos and don'ts now say to let the untargetable window pass rather than dumping the string into it, to force the R recast shield out first, and that Grievous Wounds decides the extended trade because Eviscerate keeps the pack topped up.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Now carries Hounds' Pursuit 110s at rank 1, Eviscerate 11s, The Call of the Pack 26s, Chronobreak 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] said to add anti-heal 'into his sustain' — wrong pronoun and no source for what sustains.
audit.why: Eviscerate carries the heal flag and fully heals her packmates, which is what makes extended trades hers.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal is now tied to Eviscerate by name and to her packmates being restored.

edits.before: Naafiri's early game is built to bully exactly this kind of matchup — her pack members and dash resets give her far more sustained pressure and burst than your kit has access to before level 6. Levels 1-2 you should play passively, never trading extended, since her all-in just deletes you if she commits. Levels 3-5 remain rough: her dashes chain together faster than your kit can punish, and getting caught out of position near her pack means a dead Ekko. Ward the flanks so she can't set up an unseen all-in, and lean on your jungler for early tempo.
edits.after: Naafiri's early game is built to bully exactly this matchup — packmates leap onto whatever Darkin Daggers (900 range) hits, so every trade she starts is two-on-one against your 325-range E. Levels 1-2 play passively and never trade extended, since her all-in deletes you if she commits. Levels 3-5 remain rough: Eviscerate is 11s at rank 1 and dashes out of the anomaly you set, and The Call of the Pack turns her untargetable mid-string. Ward the flanks so she can't set up unseen, and lean on your jungler for early tempo.

edits.before: Level 6 is your turning point: Chronobreak gives you a genuine answer to her all-in pattern, letting you rewind out of a bad engage or punish her over-commit with a counter-burst. Until your first item, though, still avoid initiating — let her come to you and use W's delayed stun to punish the dash-chain once she's fully committed. Look to roam when she's forced to shove or reset, since her kit offers little to punish you leaving lane compared to what she gains staying.
edits.after: Level 6 is your turning point, but it is a trade of ultimates: Chronobreak (110s) and Hounds' Pursuit (110s) come online together, so the rewind buys you the escape rather than the duel. Until your first item, avoid initiating — let her open, let the untargetable frames pass, and use W's delayed stun on the ground she has to land on. Roam when she is forced to shove or reset, since leaving lane costs you less than staying costs you here.
